claim: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neuromuscular disorder characterized by progressive weakness of almost all skeletal muscles.
source: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neuromuscular disorder characterized by progressive weakness of almost all skeletal muscles, whereas extraocular muscles (EOMs) are comparatively spared.
evidence: This is a well-established clinical characterization of ALS found in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Extraocular muscles (EOMs) are comparatively spared in ALS.
source: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neuromuscular disorder characterized by progressive weakness of almost all skeletal muscles, whereas extraocular muscles (EOMs) are comparatively spared.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Domellöf, 2019; Domellof, 2012; Ahmadi et al., 2010; Valdez et al., 2012).

claim: Hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A mice exhibit severe denervation.
source: While hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A (G93A) mice (a familial ALS mouse model) exhibit severe denervation and depletion of Pax7+satellite cells (SCs), we found that the pool of SCs and the integrity of neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) are maintained in EOMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A mice exhibit depletion of Pax7+ satellite cells.
source: While hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A (G93A) mice (a familial ALS mouse model) exhibit severe denervation and depletion of Pax7+satellite cells (SCs), we found that the pool of SCs and the integrity of neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) are maintained in EOMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The pool of satellite cells is maintained in EOMs of end-stage G93A mice.
source: While hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A (G93A) mice (a familial ALS mouse model) exhibit severe denervation and depletion of Pax7+satellite cells (SCs), we found that the pool of SCs and the integrity of neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) are maintained in EOMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The integrity of neuromuscular junctions is maintained in EOMs of end-stage G93A mice.
source: While hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of end-stage SOD1G93A (G93A) mice (a familial ALS mouse model) exhibit severe denervation and depletion of Pax7+satellite cells (SCs), we found that the pool of SCs and the integrity of neuromuscular junctions (NMJs) are maintained in EOMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: SCs derived from hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of G93A mice exhibit denervation-related activation.
source: In cell sorting profiles, SCs derived from hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of G93A mice exhibit denervation-related activation, whereas SCs from EOMs of G93A mice display spontaneous (non-denervation-related) activation, similar to SCs from wild-type mice.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3.

claim: SCs from EOMs of G93A mice display spontaneous (non-denervation-related) activation, similar to SCs from wild-type mice.
source: In cell sorting profiles, SCs derived from hindlimb and diaphragm muscles of G93A mice exhibit denervation-related activation, whereas SCs from EOMs of G93A mice display spontaneous (non-denervation-related) activation, similar to SCs from wild-type mice.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cultured EOM SCs contain more abundant transcripts of axon guidance molecules, including Cxcl12, compared to diaphragm and hindlimb counterparts.
source: Specifically, cultured EOM SCs contain more abundant transcripts of axon guidance molecules, including Cxcl12, along with more sustainable renewability than the diaphragm and hindlimb counterparts under differentiation pressure.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Cultured EOM SCs have more sustainable renewability than diaphragm and hindlimb counterparts under differentiation pressure.
source: Specifically, cultured EOM SCs contain more abundant transcripts of axon guidance molecules, including Cxcl12, along with more sustainable renewability than the diaphragm and hindlimb counterparts under differentiation pressure.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4.

claim: AAV-delivery of Cxcl12 to G93A-hindlimb SC-derived myotubes enhances motor neuron axon extension and innervation.
source: In neuromuscular co-culture assays, AAV-delivery of Cxcl12 to G93A-hindlimb SC-derived myotubes enhances motor neuron axon extension and innervation, recapitulating the innervation capacity of EOM SC-derived myotubes.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by co-culture experimental data shown in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: AAV-delivery of Cxcl12 to G93A-hindlimb SC-derived myotubes recapitulates the innervation capacity of EOM SC-derived myotubes.
source: In neuromuscular co-culture assays, AAV-delivery of Cxcl12 to G93A-hindlimb SC-derived myotubes enhances motor neuron axon extension and innervation, recapitulating the innervation capacity of EOM SC-derived myotubes.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by co-culture experimental data shown in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: G93A mice fed with sodium butyrate (NaBu) supplementation exhibited less NMJ loss in hindlimb and diaphragm muscles.
source: G93A mice fed with sodium butyrate (NaBu) supplementation exhibited less NMJ loss in hindlimb and diaphragm muscles.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: SCs derived from G93A hindlimb and diaphragm muscles displayed elevated expression of Cxcl12 following NaBu treatment in vitro.
source: Additionally, SCs derived from G93A hindlimb and diaphragm muscles displayed elevated expression of Cxcl12 and improved renewability following NaBu treatment in vitro.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: SCs derived from G93A hindlimb and diaphragm muscles displayed improved renewability following NaBu treatment in vitro.
source: Additionally, SCs derived from G93A hindlimb and diaphragm muscles displayed elevated expression of Cxcl12 and improved renewability following NaBu treatment in vitro.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: ALS results in respiratory failure and death 3–5 years following diagnosis.
source: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron (MN) loss and skeletal muscle wasting, resulting in respiratory failure and death 3–5 years following diagnosis (Hardiman et al., 2017; Vucic et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a well-established clinical fact about ALS supported by citations.

claim: The extraocular muscles (EOMs) of ALS patients exhibit comparatively preserved structure and function.
source: While not entirely spared, the extraocular muscles (EOMs) of ALS patients and mutant mouse models exhibit comparatively preserved structure and function and retained neuromuscular junctions (NMJ; Domellöf, 2019; Domellof, 2012; Ahmadi et al., 2010; Valdez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The extraocular muscles (EOMs) of mutant mouse models exhibit comparatively preserved structure and function.
source: While not entirely spared, the extraocular muscles (EOMs) of ALS patients and mutant mouse models exhibit comparatively preserved structure and function and retained neuromuscular junctions (NMJ; Domellöf, 2019; Domellof, 2012; Ahmadi et al., 2010; Valdez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Eye movements are preferentially involved in myasthenia gravis.
source: The reason for this differential involvement remains unclear, especially considering that eye movements are preferentially involved in other neuromuscular disorders like myasthenia gravis, some muscular dystrophies, and mitochondrial myopathies (Greaves et al., 2010; Soltys et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Eye movements are preferentially involved in some muscular dystrophies.
source: The reason for this differential involvement remains unclear, especially considering that eye movements are preferentially involved in other neuromuscular disorders like myasthenia gravis, some muscular dystrophies, and mitochondrial myopathies (Greaves et al., 2010; Soltys et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Eye movements are preferentially involved in mitochondrial myopathies.
source: The reason for this differential involvement remains unclear, especially considering that eye movements are preferentially involved in other neuromuscular disorders like myasthenia gravis, some muscular dystrophies, and mitochondrial myopathies (Greaves et al., 2010; Soltys et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Early muscle dysfunction is an important contributor to ALS pathophysiology.
source: While ALS is classically considered predominantly a 'dying-forward' process of motor neurons (MN), accumulated evidence (Luo et al., 2013; Yi et al., 2021; Zhou et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2010b; Xiao et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2018; Dobrowolny et al., 2008; Wong and Martin, 2010; Loeffler et al., 2016) support that early muscle dysfunction is an important contributor to ALS pathophysiology.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: NMJ disassembly and the resulting skeletal muscle denervation is a critical pathogenic event in ALS patients and animal models.
source: Regardless of the direction of communication and relative contribution of different cell types to ALS progression (e.g. glia, neurons, myofibers; Frey et al., 2000), it is widely accepted that NMJ disassembly and the resulting skeletal muscle denervation is a critical pathogenic event in both patients and animal models (Campanari et al., 2019; Cappello and Francolini, 2017; Clark et al., 2016; Martineau et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: EOMs express both adult fast and slow myosin contractile elements.
source: Besides the developmental myosin isoforms, EOMs also express both adult fast and slow myosin contractile elements (Zhou et al., 2010a), suggesting that the sparing may not be solely linked to the fast or slow twitch nature of the muscle fibers, rather the changes in SCs may play a pivotal role in preserving the EOM function during the progression of ALS.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Individual motor neurons controlling EOMs innervate fewer EOM myofibers compared to other skeletal muscles.
source: In contrast to other skeletal muscles, the individual motor neurons (MNs) controlling EOMs innervate fewer EOM myofibers, and individual myofibers often have multiple NMJs (Nijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Individual EOM myofibers often have multiple NMJs.
source: In contrast to other skeletal muscles, the individual motor neurons (MNs) controlling EOMs innervate fewer EOM myofibers, and individual myofibers often have multiple NMJs (Nijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Each EOM myofiber has one 'en plaque' NMJ.
source: The 'en plaque' type of NMJs are located in the middle portion of myofibers and resemble NMJs seen in other types of muscles. Each EOM myofiber has one 'un plaque' NMJ.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a description of EOM NMJ structure.

claim: 'En grappe' NMJs are located in the distal portion of some EOM myofibers.
source: 'en grappe' NMJs are a series of smaller, grape-shaped NMJs that are located in the distal portion of some EOM myofibers (Domellöf, 2019; Nijssen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MNs innervating EOMs express higher level of the Ca2+ binding proteins calbindin-D28k and parvalbumin.
source: MNs innervating EOMs express higher level of the Ca2+ binding proteins calbindin-D28k and parvalbumin, thus may be more resistant to the Ca2+-induced excitotoxicity (Ince et al., 1993; Alexianu et al., 1994; Mosier et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: MNs innervating EOMs may be more resistant to Ca2+-induced excitotoxicity.
source: MNs innervating EOMs express higher level of the Ca2+ binding proteins calbindin-D28k and parvalbumin, thus may be more resistant to the Ca2+-induced excitotoxicity (Ince et al., 1993; Alexianu et al., 1994; Mosier et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference based on the expression of Ca2+ binding proteins, supported by citations.

claim: Pronounced differences exist between EOM and limb muscles in their transcriptomic profiles.
source: Pronounced differences exist between EOM and limb muscles in their transcriptomic profiles (Fischer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: More than 2500 proteins are differentially expressed between EOM and EDL muscles.
source: In addition, a recent proteomic study revealed more than 2500 proteins differentially expressed between EOM and EDL muscles and more than 2000 between EOM and soleus muscles (Eckhardt et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: More than 2000 proteins are differentially expressed between EOM and soleus muscles.
source: In addition, a recent proteomic study revealed more than 2500 proteins differentially expressed between EOM and EDL muscles and more than 2000 between EOM and soleus muscles (Eckhardt et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Muscle-derived neuroprotective factors (BDNF, GDNF, NT3, NT4) were not expressed significantly higher in EOM myofibers compared to hindlimb myofibers in G93A and wild-type mice.
source: However, none of muscle-derived neuroprotective factors, including BDNF, GDNF, NT3, and NT4 were expressed (RNA or proteins) significantly higher in EOM myofibers compared to hindlimb myofibers in both mutant G93A and wild-type mice (Eckhardt et al., 2023; Harandi et al., 2014; Harandi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Inducible depletion of adult skeletal muscle SCs impaired the regeneration of NMJs.
source: Using transgenic mice expressing GFP in the progeny of activated SCs, Liu and colleagues demonstrated that inducible depletion of adult skeletal muscle SCs impaired the regeneration of NMJs (Liu et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of SCs exacerbated age-related NMJ degeneration.
source: Furthermore, they found that the loss of SCs exacerbated age-related NMJ degeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to findings by Liu and colleagues.

claim: Preservation of SCs attenuated aging-related NMJ loss and improved muscle performance in mice.
source: Preservation of SCs attenuated aging-related NMJ loss and improved muscle performance in mice (Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: SCs from EOMs exhibit superior expansion and renewability than their limb counterparts.
source: SCs from EOMs exhibit superior expansion and renewability (the capability to maintain dividing and undifferentiated stem cells after rounds of regeneration) than their limb counterparts (Stuelsatz et al., 2015), inspiring us to compare the phenotypes of SCs derived from EOMs and limb muscles and to conduct transcriptomic profiling of SCs to look for candidate genes that could preserve NMJ integrity in ALS.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: EDL, soleus and diaphragm muscles from end stage G93A mice exhibited significant decrease in well-innervated NMJs.
source: EDL, soleus and diaphragm muscles, but not EOMs, from end stage G93A mice (4-month-old) exhibited significant decrease in well-innervated NMJs, accompanied by an increase in poorly-innervate NMJs.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: EDL, soleus and diaphragm muscles from end stage G93A mice exhibited an increase in poorly-innervated NMJs.
source: EDL, soleus and diaphragm muscles, but not EOMs, from end stage G93A mice (4-month-old) exhibited significant decrease in well-innervated NMJs, accompanied by an increase in poorly-innervate NMJs.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: EOMs from end stage G93A mice did not exhibit significant decrease in well-innervated NMJs.
source: EDL, soleus and diaphragm muscles, but not EOMs, from end stage G93A mice (4-month-old) exhibited significant decrease in well-innervated NMJs, accompanied by an increase in poorly-innervate NMJs.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Denervation process is most severe in hindlimb muscles, slightly milder in diaphragm and barely detectable in EOMs.
source: The increase of 'poorly-innervated NMJ' is slightly less dramatic in diaphragm compared to the hindlimb muscles, meanwhile the increase of 'partially-innervated NMJ' ratio is the most significant in the diaphragm (Figure 1B), indicating that denervation process is most severe in hindlimb muscles, slightly milder in diaphragm and barely detectable in EOMs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data stated in the results section and supported by Figure 1B.

claim: NaBu treatment started after disease onset was effective in preserving NMJ integrity in G93A mice.
source: As the treatment for ALS patients is initiated after symptoms appear, we further tested whether NaBu treatment started after the disease onset (at the age of 3 months, 2% NaBu in water for 1 month) was effective in preserving NMJ integrity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Hindlimb and diaphragm muscles from NaBu-fed G93A mice exhibited significantly reduced denervation compared to littermates who were not fed NaBu.
source: Consistent with previous observation, the hindlimb and diaphragm muscles from NaBu-fed mice (1 month, 2% in water, starting to feed at the age of 3-month-old) all exhibited significantly reduced denervation compared to littermates who were not fed NaBu (Figure 1B, n=10 per group, gender matched).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Scn5a expression elevation is most notable when comparing G93A hindlimb muscles to wildtype counterparts.
source: Consistent with the immunostaining quantification in Figure 1A, the elevation of Scn5a expression is most notable when comparing G93A hindlimb muscles to wildtype counterparts (>250 folds for EDL, >70 folds for soleus), milder for diaphragm (>15 folds) and not significant for EOMs.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NaBu feeding significantly reduced Scn5a transcripts in hindlimb muscles.
source: Additionally, NaBu feeding significantly reduced the Scn5a transcripts in hindlimb muscles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was most significant in hindlimb muscles of end-stage G93A mice.
source: Similar to the NMJ denervation status, depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was most significant in hindlimb muscles of end-stage G93A mice and slightly milder in diaphragm, while no significant depletion was observed in EOMs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was slightly milder in diaphragm of end-stage G93A mice compared to hindlimb muscles.
source: Similar to the NMJ denervation status, depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was most significant in hindlimb muscles of end-stage G93A mice and slightly milder in diaphragm, while no significant depletion was observed in EOMs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: No significant depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was observed in EOMs of end-stage G93A mice.
source: Similar to the NMJ denervation status, depletion of peri-NMJ SCs was most significant in hindlimb muscles of end-stage G93A mice and slightly milder in diaphragm, while no significant depletion was observed in EOMs (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: G93A mice fed with NaBu had less depletion of SCs in hindlimb and diaphragm muscles.
source: G93A mice fed with NaBu had less depletion of SCs in hindlimb and diaphragm muscles.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: SCs isolated from WT hindlimb and diaphragm muscles exhibited relatively homogenous levels of Vcam1.
source: SCs isolated from WT hindlimb and diaphragm muscles exhibited relatively homogenous levels of Vcam1, which facilitated separation from other cells and debris (Figure 3A, gate P5-4), and also indicates they are mostly quiescent under resting conditions.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SCs isolated from WT hindlimb and diaphragm muscles are mostly quiescent under resting conditions.
source: SCs isolated from WT hindlimb and diaphragm muscles exhibited relatively homogenous levels of Vcam1, which facilitated separation from other cells and debris (Figure 3A, gate P5-4), and also indicates they are mostly quiescent under resting conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SCs derived from G93A hindlimb and diaphragm displayed heterogeneous levels of Vcam1.
source: In contrast, SCs derived from the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm displayed heterogeneous levels of Vcam1, potentially due to ongoing activation/differentiation triggered by disease progression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Heterogeneous Vcam1 levels in G93A hindlimb and diaphragm SCs are potentially due to ongoing activation/differentiation triggered by disease progression.
source: In contrast, SCs derived from the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm displayed heterogeneous levels of Vcam1, potentially due to ongoing activation/differentiation triggered by disease progression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the results section based on FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: EOM SCs from both WT and G93A mice were heterogeneous in Vcam1 levels.
source: Importantly, EOM SCs from both WT and G93A mice were heterogeneous in Vcam1 levels, implying they are spontaneously activated even in the absence of pathological stimulation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: EOM SCs are spontaneously activated even in the absence of pathological stimulation.
source: Importantly, EOM SCs from both WT and G93A mice were heterogeneous in Vcam1 levels, implying they are spontaneously activated even in the absence of pathological stimulation (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on FACS data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Significant decreases of P5-4 population were observed in G93A hindlimb and diaphragm-derived SCs compared to WT.
source: While significant decreases of P5-4 population were observed in the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm-derived SCs compared to WT, no significant difference was detected between G93A and WT EOM-derived SCs (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No significant difference in P5-4 population was detected between G93A and WT EOM-derived SCs.
source: While significant decreases of P5-4 population were observed in the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm-derived SCs compared to WT, no significant difference was detected between G93A and WT EOM-derived SCs (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Close to 100% of FACS-isolated SCs cultured for 4 days were MyoD positive.
source: FACS-isolated SCs were next cultured in growth medium for 4 days, fixed, and stained for MyoD to confirm their myogenic lineage. Close to 100% of the cells were MyoD positive (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SCs isolated from both WT and G93A EOMs exhibited the highest Pax7+/Ki67+ ratio.
source: SCs isolated from both WT and G93A EOMs exhibited the highest Pax/Ki67 double positive ratio, and the lowest Pax7/Ki67 double negative ratio (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: SCs isolated from both WT and G93A EOMs exhibited the lowest Pax7-/Ki67- ratio.
source: SCs isolated from both WT and G93A EOMs exhibited the highest Pax/Ki67 double positive ratio, and the lowest Pax7/Ki67 double negative ratio (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: EOM SCs have superior proliferative potential compared to limb and diaphragm muscles.
source: These observations are consistent with previous reports of superior proliferative potential of EOM SCs compared to limb and diaphragm muscles (Stuelsatz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation and the data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: EOM-derived SCs exhibited a higher number of Pax7-positive cells compared to SCs derived from hindlimb and diaphragm muscles under differentiation conditions.
source: The EOM-derived SCs exhibited a higher number of Pax7-positive cells (Pax7+/Ki67+ and Pax7+/Ki67-) compared to SCs derived from hindlimb and diaphragm muscles – from both WT and G93A mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The fusion indices were the lowest for EOM SCs under differentiation conditions.
source: In contrast, the fusion indices, which calculate the ratio of nucleus within the MHC-positive myotubes, were the lowest for EOM SCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The low fusion index of EOM SCs is likely a reflection of their superior preservation of actively proliferating population.
source: This does not necessarily mean the EOM SCs have deficiencies in differentiation after they are committed, but more likely a reflection of their superior preservation of actively proliferating population (Ancel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on immunostaining data and supported by a citation.

claim: More myofibers were generated by EOM SCs than their limb counterparts in TA engraftment experiments.
source: In support of this view, previous TA engraftment experiments showed that more myofibers were generated by EOM SCs than their limb counterparts (Stuelsatz et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by a citation.

claim: The relative expression of proliferation markers (Hmhg2 and Ccnd1) in G93A hindlimb SCs peaked at 0.5 mM NaBu.
source: The relative expression of the proliferation markers (Hmhg2 and Ccnd1) peaked at 0.5 mM.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The relative expression of proliferation inhibitor P21 in G93A hindlimb SCs bottomed at 0.5 mM NaBu.
source: In contrast, the relative expression of proliferation inhibitor P21 bottomed at 0.5 mM (Figure 5A), indicating 0.5 mM as the optimal concentration of NaBu application in vitro.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: 0.5 mM is the optimal concentration of NaBu application in vitro for G93A hindlimb SCs.
source: In contrast, the relative expression of proliferation inhibitor P21 bottomed at 0.5 mM (Figure 5A), indicating 0.5 mM as the optimal concentration of NaBu application in vitro.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: G93A hindlimb and diaphragm SCs showed significant increase in the ratio of Pax7-positive cells under 1-day NaBu treatment.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm SCs in culture showed significant increase in the ratio of Pax7-positive cells under the 1-day NaBu treatment, associated with a decrease in fusion index.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: 1-day NaBu treatment of G93A hindlimb and diaphragm SCs was associated with a decrease in fusion index.
source: As shown in Figure 5B, the G93A hindlimb and diaphragm SCs in culture showed significant increase in the ratio of Pax7-positive cells under the 1-day NaBu treatment, associated with a decrease in fusion index.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The trend of increased Pax7-positive cells and decreased fusion index was more pronounced under 3-day NaBu treatment.
source: This trend was more pronounced under the 3-day NaBu treatment.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: NaBu treatment results in EOM-like preservation of renewability of G93A SCs.
source: These data indicate that NaBu treatment results in EOM-like preservation of renewability of the G93A SCs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Long-term exposure to NaBu inhibited the differentiation process of G93A SCs.
source: Aside from the drop of fusion indices after 3-day treatment with NaBu, there was notable decrease of MHC levels, indicating long-term exposure to NaBu did inhibit the differentiation process (Figure 5B), which is in line with the published result observed in myoblasts of different origins (Iezzi et al., 2002; Fiszman et al., 1980; Johnston et al., 1992).
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section and supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B and citations.

claim: Both WT and G93A EOM SCs cultured in differentiation medium were more similar to hindlimb and diaphragm SCs in growth medium than their counterparts in differentiation medium.
source: We found that both WT and G93A EOM SCs cultured in differentiation medium were more similar to hindlimb and diaphragm SCs in growth medium than their counterparts in differentiation medium, highlighting the superior renewability of EOM SCs in differentiation medium and is consistent with the immunostaining results showed in Figure 4B.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section based on PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cultured WT and G93A SCs from the same muscle origins exhibited relatively similar gross transcriptomic profiles.
source: Considering that cultured WT and G93A SCs from the same muscle origins exhibited relatively similar gross transcriptomic profiles in PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis, and that the proliferation and differentiation properties of cultured WT and G93A SCs from the same muscles were only marginally different in immunofluorescence assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we speculate that the differential homeostasis seen in the FACS profiles of hindlimb and diaphragm SCs (Figure 3) may relate to the pathological milieu in vivo.
evidence: This is a finding stated in the results section based on PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The differential homeostasis seen in the FACS profiles of hindlimb and diaphragm SCs may relate to the pathological milieu in vivo.
source: Considering that cultured WT and G93A SCs from the same muscle origins exhibited relatively similar gross transcriptomic profiles in PCA and hierarchical clustering analysis, and that the proliferation and differentiation properties of cultured WT and G93A SCs from the same muscles were only marginally different in immunofluorescence assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), we speculate that the differential homeostasis seen in the FACS profiles of hindlimb and diaphragm SCs (Figure 3) may relate to the pathological milieu in vivo.
evidence: This is a speculation stated in the results section based on RNA-Seq and immunostaining data.

claim: When G93A SCs are isolated and cultured in vitro, their properties become similar to those of WT counterparts.
source: When G93A SCs are isolated and cultured in vitro, their properties become similar to those of WT counterparts.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section based on RNA-Seq and immunostaining data.

claim: Top 20 DEGs comparing EOM SCs to their hindlimb and diaphragm counterparts are mainly homeobox transcription factors.
